name: Pasach
overview: Pasach is a male figure from the tribe of Asher, identified specifically as the son of Japhlet. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or details beyond his lineage in 1 Chronicles 7:33. This establishes him within the genealogical records important for understanding the tribal heritage of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Pasach is a proper name meaning 'to divide.' This meaning is noted but not explicitly connected to any narrative or theological significance in the biblical text. It is not indicated that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Pasach is explicitly recorded as the son of Japhlet, linking him to the family line within the tribe of Asher. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family connections or descendants for Pasach.
scriptureSignificance: Pasach's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Asher, as documented in 1 Chronicles 7:33. While there are no recorded deeds or events associated with him, his inclusion helps preserve the continuity of Israel's tribal history. This genealogical detail contributes to the broader biblical narrative of God's covenant people and their tribal identities.
